description: Very expressive multilingual TTS (80+ languages). Steer delivery with [tags] in the text: [sighs], [whispering]. Clones from a clip plus its transcript. Needs about 43 GB of VRAM, but runs on as little as 8 GB by offloading to RAM, at the cost of speed. Free under US$500k revenue.

workerSettings.label: GPU memory target (GB)
workerSettings.description: How much memory Drama 3 may use on each GPU. The settings below that are on Auto are switched on, in order, until it fits. 0 = the whole GPU (other workers loaded on it aren't counted). If it can't fit, the worker log says so and it tries anyway.

workerSettings.label: Expert precision
workerSettings.description: 4-bit re-quantizes the model's experts while loading: about 29 GB instead of 43, at some loss of quality. Auto: FP8 when it fits without any of the settings below, otherwise 4-bit.

workerSettings.label: Expert layers in RAM
workerSettings.description: Keeps the experts of this many of the 40 layers in system RAM and copies the ones each step needs to the GPU (about 0.4 GB less GPU memory per layer with 4-bit experts, about 0.75 with FP8). Slower: about 0.6x real time with all 40 on one 24 GB GPU. Needs as much free RAM. With a GPU count of 1 only.

workerSettings.label: Codec
workerSettings.description: Where reference clips are encoded and audio is decoded. The CPU leaves about 2 GB more on the GPU and takes a few seconds longer per segment. On the GPU it still falls back to the CPU when the GPU runs out of memory.

workerSettings.label: 8-bit attention and audio decoder
workerSettings.description: Stores the attention and audio decoder weights in 8 bits: about 2 GB less GPU memory, a little slower, possibly a little less like the reference voice. With a GPU count of 1 only.

settings.label: Reference transcript
settings.description: The exact words spoken in the reference clip. Required for cloning. Without a reference clip the model invents a different voice for every segment.
